description: Hi, we're team miguel! We're just 2 students from SUTD trying to win this hackathon by creating something meaningful :)
summary:
MarsXMoon: Artifact Explorer is an interactive 3D web application developed by us to gamify the history of space exploration, designed to target teenagers from ages 12-17. We developed a browser-based educational experience where users navigate 3D models of the Moon and Mars to discover discarded NASA equipment. By employing an engaging "excavation" mechanic, players use their cursor to physically brush away dust to reveal historical artifacts—like the Apollo descent stages or the Opportunity rover—unlocking detailed lore, mission data, and coordinates.
This addresses the "NASA's Discarded Equipment Storytelling" challenge by transforming static historical archives into an immersive, character-guided journey. Rather than reading a standard timeline of space debris, users interact with anthropomorphized anime-girl planet guides (Moon-chan and Mars-chan) and test their knowledge through a dynamic, randomized quiz system. This project is important because it bridges the gap between complex space history and public engagement, making the legacy of NASA's robotic and human explorers accessible, memorable, and fun for all.
details:
What our project does and how it works: The application renders 3D planetary models that users can rotate and zoom into using their mouse. Turquoise markers indicate the landing sites of abandoned spacecraft. Clicking a marker brings up an interactive "dusty" card. Using an HTML5 Canvas integration, users must use their cursor as an archaeological brush to scrub away the lunar or Martian dust. Once cleared, an unlock sound plays, and the artifact's historical data is revealed. After uncovering all artifacts on a planet, users unlock the ability to travel to the next planet or take a randomized trivia quiz to test their knowledge.


Benefits and Intended Impact: The primary benefit is making space history highly tactile and interactive. The intended impact is to educate the general public and students about NASA's legacy in a way that feels like a video game rather than a textbook, increasing retention and interest in space sciences.

Tools and Technologies: The project was developed using React, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), and React Three Drei (@react-three/drei). We utilized standard web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) alongside custom audio files for BGM and SFX.

How our project is creative: We gamified the experience by introducing anime-inspired, anthropomorphized guides who break the fourth wall and provide a narrative framework. The dusting mechanic provides a tactile satisfaction that standard UI buttons lack, and the UI dynamically shifts themes (colors and dialogue boxes) based on whether the user is on the Moon or Mars.

Factors the team considered: We carefully considered user experience and modern browser limitations. For example, we built a dedicated "Begin Exploration" start screen to comply with strict browser audio autoplay policies, ensuring our custom SFX and BGM play flawlessly. We also prioritized educational accuracy, pulling coordinate data and mission lore directly from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) and NASA's official mission pages.
